title: Pilot sync - token leakage and adaptive retry plan
next_steps: Redwood to share debug bundle and telemetry URLs by 2027-12-10
Nimbus to run targeted traffic pattern (burst + long-tail) next Tue and share logs
Schedule private cluster benchmark with 5M token corpus week of 2027-12-13
SE to propose adaptive retry config (3 variants) by 2027-12-12
action_items: Maya Singh - collect server-side traces for 5xx spikes - 2027-12-10
Rajiv Patel - export nginx + client retry traces and share dropbox link - 2027-12-11
Jesse Park - send security one-pager and SOC2 summar y - 2027-12-09
Tom Wu - validate KV cache hit rate on pilot nodes - 2027-12-14
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on two emergent reliability issues: (1) apparent token leakage causing larger-than-expected per-request token counts and occasional timeouts; (2) intermittent 5xx bursts correlated with hot-key traffic and aggressive client retries. Redwood SE walked through telemetry, proposed adaptive retry/backoff presets, and agreed next steps for shared benchmarks and targeted logging. Nimbus requested additional audit logs and SOC2 short summary before approving private cluster benchmark.
topics: token leakage, timeouts, 5xx spikes, rate limits, adaptive retries, KV cache, telemetry gaps, SOC2/audit logs, private benchmark
transcript:
[14:00] Meeting started. Auto-generated note: recording enabled.
[14:00] Jesse Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining the weekly pilot sync. we know last week you hit those sporadic 502/504s and a few unexpected token counts, so we want to go over what we saw and propose a plan.
[14:01] Lena Ortiz: thanks jesse. quick note, we pulled a sample of 200 requests and a small subset had token counts 2-3x what our client computed, causing our rate windows to blow past limits. we suspect either prompt concatenation on client or an upstream tokenization mismatch.
[14:02] Rajiv Patel: yea and on top of that the client SDK was retrying aggressively which amplified the hotspot. our ingress logged many concurrent attempts that mirrored the same payload id.
[14:03] Maya Singh: ok, two parallel threads: token accounting mismatch and retry amplification. on the token side, we instrumented tokenization at the runtime and saw occasional off-by-one + added system prompt duplicated when long chat histories were proxied through our caching layer.
[14:04] Tom Wu: duplicated how? are you saying the prefix was replayed?
[14:04] Maya Singh: sometimes the prefix from cache wasn't cleared; it's subtle — a race when a KV cache entry was refreshed concurrently with a request. the payload that hits the model includes both cached prefix+fresh context, so effective tokens go up.
[14:05] Paul (contractor): that matches an incident we saw where the client sent same conversation twice because of a UI double-tap, so both client and server factors.
[14:06] Lena Ortiz: hmm. so it might be both. what's your mitigation recommendation short-term?
[14:06] Maya Singh: immediate mitigation: 1) conservative dedupe on the client id at the edge for 200ms, 2) server-side check: if cached prefix present, ensure it's applied idempotently (add simple hashing guard), 3) temporary tightening of token accounting alert thresholds so you catch >1.5x anomalies early.
[14:07] Jesse Park: and for the 5xx spikes we correlated, during those windows the retry storms amplified a hot-key — lots of identical requests for the same model+route. our suggestion is adaptive retry windows: implement a per-route circuit-breaker that disables retries for routes experiencing >3% 5xx within 30s and switch clients to a slower exponential backoff.
[14:08] Rajiv Patel: our current client implement doubles every 200ms up to 6 retries, which is brutal on backpressure. we need guidance on backoff curves that respect latency SLO.
[14:09] Maya Singh: propose three presets: optimistic (base 100ms, cap 500ms, 2 retries), balanced (base 200ms, cap 2s, 3 retries), conservative (base 500ms, cap 5s, 1 retry). also server will expose a Retry-Recommended header when route is under stress so clients can opt in.
[14:10] Anna Meyer: if we flip to conservative, user-facing latency suffers. product is worried. can you simulate user impact?
[14:11] Jesse Park: yes, we'll run a shadow traffic benchmark with your sample traces and measure p99 latency for the presets. that’s one of the scheduled next steps.
[14:12] Lena Ortiz: what about rate limiting? we saw token budget blowouts because token accounting mismatch made us hit rate windows and then the infra returned 429, causing retries — a classic loop.
[14:13] Maya Singh: right — add server-side token-bucket smoothing: when token consumption spike is detected, server will stall new requests for short tail (20-100ms) to smooth peaks and return a Retry-After header for clients configured to respect it. it reduces tail spikes without wholesale hard 429s.
[14:14] Rajiv Patel: can Redwood control that without breaking our SLA?
[14:14] Jesse Park: smoothing is opt-in for Dedicated and Private pilots; for hosted we can enable in your tenant with agreed thresholds. SLA implications are small because it's designed to avoid cascading failures; we'll document expected behavior.
[14:15] Tom Wu: telemetry — we saw gaps. there were windows with missing per-token emit data. why?
[14:16] Maya Singh: two causes: (1) small sampling bug in our telemetry collector when aggregate payloads exceed 256kb, some events were dropped; (2) the agent on your infra was set to low verbosity. we patched the sampler yesterday and will push a fix to avoid the 256kb truncation.
[14:17] Lena Ortiz: can you provide a test bundle we can run to validate the fix?
[14:17] Maya Singh: yes, we’ll give you a debug bundle plus steps.
[14:18] Paul: also, can we get more granular audit logs for token use per-tenant? Security wants them for compliance.
[14:19] Jesse Park: yes, we can enable extended audit logs for the pilot — adds storage cost but can be toggled. we'll include a short SOC2 summary with controls mapped to your needs.
[14:20] Anna Meyer: product question: how visible will the KV cache hits be? we want to know hit/miss per conversation so we can tune UI stitching.
[14:20] Maya Singh: we'll surface KV cache metrics (hit/miss rate, application latency) in the Console route dashboard and expose them through the API.
[14:21] Rajiv Patel: when you mentioned duplicate prefixes there was talk about a race; is that a code path we can patch quickly or does it require a runtime rollout?
[14:22] Maya Singh: it's a small guard change in the cache apply path; for hosted we can hotfix and roll in a patch behind a flag; for Private you'd apply the patch during your maintenance window. estimated turnaround: 48–72 hours to ship and validate.
[14:23] Tom Wu: for Private deployment benchmark we want to run model with 300 concurrent streams of average 800 tokens, plus synthetic double-send events. can Redwood run that?
[14:24] Jesse Park: yes, we'll coordinate a private cluster benchmark with our infra team. need confirmed maintenance window and a dataset — you mentioned a 5M token corpus earlier?
[14:25] Anna Meyer: yes, we can provide a scrubbed corpus. security will need the SOC2 summary before greenlighting.
[14:26] Jesse Park: understood. we'll send SOC2 summary and template for scrub confirmation.
[14:27] Rajiv Patel: on retries, will you provide client SDK changes or just server guidance and headers?
[14:28] Maya Singh: we'll provide both: guidance + client SDK patch that honors Retry-Recommended and Retry-After headers and supports the three presets. we can ship a minimal patch to your Node clients in a week.
[14:29] Lena Ortiz: about the 5xx stack traces we asked for last week — any new insights?
[14:29] Maya Singh: after correlating traces we saw 60% of 5xx windows align with GC pauses on a small subset of nodes and 35% with hot-key eviction thrash. remaining 5% unknown, we're collecting more telemetry. GC tune + cache eviction tunables reduce some spikes.
[14:30] Jesse Park: action item: we'll provide tuned GC settings for the pilot cluster and a list of cache eviction params to try.
[14:31] Tom Wu: do you expect the token leakage fix to reduce 5xxs?
[14:32] Maya Singh: it should — fewer tokens per request means lower compute per request and reduced queueing; combined with adaptive retries it reduces amplification.
[14:33] Anna Meyer: any immediate rollback/fallback if the hotkey returns?
[14:33] Jesse Park: yes — we recommend a conditional fallback to a cheaper model variant if latency/p99 crosses a threshold. fallback logic: if p99 > 2s for a route for 60s, route to quantized variant with warning header.
[14:34] Rajiv Patel: can that be per-customer? we don't want other customers to be affected.
[14:35] Jesse Park: per-tenant routing is supported in Dedicated and Private; hosted we can configure per-tenant as well. it's part of the rollout policy.
[14:36] Lena Ortiz: quick note on observability: can we have per-request owner metadata so we can join logs with our upstream traces?
[14:36] Maya Singh: yes, we support passing X-Request-Id and will surface it in logs and traces. ensure your client sets it.
[14:37] Paul: small nit — sometimes Firefy (sic) transcriptions show Redwood product as Redwood Inference, but in our notes people wrote "RedwoodSrv" which made search hard.
[14:38] Jesse Park: ha, noted.
[14:38] Anna Meyer: can we get a quick recap of concrete steps and owners now?
[14:39] Jesse Park: sure. recap: (1) Redwood send debug bundle + telemetry links (Jesse) by Fri 12/10; (2) SE patch for KV cache guard and telemetry sampler fix (Maya) by 12/10–12/11; (3) Nimbus runs targeted traffic test Tue and shares logs (Rajiv) by 12/11; (4) Redwood propose 3 retry presets and provide client SDK patch (Maya) by 12/12; (5) SOC2 summary and audit logs enablement (Jesse) by 12/09; (6) private cluster benchmark scheduling (cross-team) by 12/13.
[14:40] Lena Ortiz: thanks. one last ask — can you include expected cost delta when enabling extended audit logs? we need finance approval.
[14:41] Jesse Park: yes, we'll include estimated storage and egress cost delta in the follow-up.
[14:42] Rajiv Patel: ok, that sounds good. any blockers?
[14:42] Maya Singh: main blocker is getting scrubbed corpus and SOC2 signoff. once those aligned we can run benchmark.
[14:43] Anna Meyer: we'll prioritize SOC2 review this week.
[14:44] Jesse Park: awesome. we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark and send the debug bundle. thanks everyone.
[14:45] Meeting ended.
notes: Telemetry fixes pushed to staging; Redwood to run targeted benchmark after SOC2 confirmation. Client to reduce retry aggressiveness pending SDK patch.
